_notes: Every entry here is a REAL, verifiable national institution — not a sample/placeholder private business directory. Unlike buyer_directory.json (which uses illustrative sample entries), this file intentionally does NOT invent specific private cold-storage or transport company names/phone numbers, because those cannot be verified and a wrong number here could waste a farmer's time trying to move perishable produce. Every entry has a real sourceUrl a farmer or developer can check. If real local/state warehouse contact data becomes available (e.g. a live WDRA registered-warehouse feed), replace the state-level generic entries below with actual per-district listings.

national.name: Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC)
national.description: Government of India warehousing body (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution) operating 700+ warehouses nationwide, including cold storage and temperature-controlled facilities at many locations.
national.verificationStatus: CONFIRMED — official CWC toll-free number and website.

national.name: WDRA Registered Warehouse Locator
national.description: Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority maintains the official list of registered warehouses (incl. cold storage) by state and district — the most reliable way to find a real, regulated facility near you.
national.contactInfo: Search by state/district on the WDRA portal

national.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Cold Storage Financing
national.description: Central government financing scheme (via NABARD/banks) for setting up or expanding cold storage, warehousing, and post-harvest infrastructure — relevant to FPOs/farmer groups planning shared storage, not just for individual storage bookings.
national.contactInfo: Apply via participating banks or NABARD
national.verificationStatus: CONFIRMED — official NABARD scheme reference. Confirm current terms directly, as financing scheme conditions change.

howToFindLocalTransport.note: This app does not maintain a directory of private local transport/trucking contacts, since these change often and cannot be centrally verified the way a national institution can. Recommended real steps instead:
steps: Ask your buyer or FPO — many buyer listings in the Sell For Profit page already include a location; local transport is often arranged by the buyer or the APMC yard itself.
Check with your nearest APMC (Agricultural Produce Market Committee) yard — they typically maintain lists of registered local transporters.
Ask your Village Agriculture Officer or nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) — they often know reliable local operators.
